questions.q: Which mechanism limits the scope and duration of an automated action?
questions.explain: Guardrails bound the impact of an error: scope, duration, approval, and reversibility.

questions.q: Match each use case to its effect.

pairs.right: Repeatable deployment of VMs or cloud accounts

questions.explain: These five use cases cover identity, resources, configuration, detection, and tracking.

questions.q: Which AI capability is absent from the four textbooks but required by objective 4.6?
questions.explain: Agentic AI, capable of executing actions autonomously, is not covered in the provided textbooks. Flagged as beyond-textbooks in objective 4.6.

questions.q: Which elements are part of considerations before automating? (Select all that apply)
questions.explain: Logging is mandatory: removing audit trails increases risk instead of reducing it.

questions.q: What is the difference between automation and orchestration?
options: Orchestration coordinates multiple tools in an end-to-end workflow
Automation is always performed by agentic AI
questions.explain: Automation targets a single task; orchestration chains multiple tasks and tools into a scenario.

questions.q: In an IP-blocking playbook, what should be done after the action itself?
options: Verify the effect, monitor for false positives, and tune the rule
Expand the block to the entire network
questions.explain: The loop closes with verification and continuous improvement of the playbook.
